Desktop login environment

The login race that can start ChatGPT without the gateway, the managed login agent that closes it, and what desktop status reports about it.

About 5 min read · 5 sections

On this page
01 The login environment agent 02 Standalone registration 03 API mode 04 Rollback and removal 05 Checking login status

Part of the Codex app-server adapter, and a section of the native relay guide.

The login environment agent

ChatGPT is a login item and can start before the unified service has set CODEX_CLI_PATH. When that happens the app launches its own bundled engine and runs without the gateway until it is restarted; this was seen on a Mac that rebooted after a power outage.

With the unified service (0.4.8 and later) the gateway has one background item, harness-gateway, and no separate agent. The service daemon closes the race itself: its very first step, before consolidation, any wait, the network or any child, is /bin/launchctl setenv CODEX_CLI_PATH <registered wrapper>. It runs only when desktop-registration.json names this gateway's own wrapper (the same ownership proof registration uses), the wrapper is executable, the release runtime exists, and the login session holds no value or one of the gateway's own wrappers. A foreign override is never replaced. A failure never stops the daemon: it records one desktop_env_preset_failed event with a fixed reason (read or setenv, see diagnostics), never a value or a path. The desktop-restore child that runs at every service start no longer writes the agent; it removes a managed one that 0.4.7 left, so a 0.4.7 Mac loses the harness-gateway-login-env item at its first 0.4.8 start. A plist at that label without the gateway's marker is left alone and reported as unmanaged.

Standalone registration

Standalone registration (no unified service and no pending login plan) keeps the agent described below. To close the race there, registration also writes a small LaunchAgent, com.edihasaj.subscription-gateway.desktop-env. It runs one command at login and exits. macOS names a background item after the program a LaunchAgent runs, so the agent does not run launchctl directly (Login Items would list "launchctl"). Its only program argument is a private script in the gateway state directory, harness-gateway-login-env, which Login Items lists by that name:

#!/bin/sh
# Managed by subscription-gateway desktop-env
exec /bin/launchctl setenv CODEX_CLI_PATH '<state>/desktop-wrapper-<hash>'

It has RunAtLoad, no KeepAlive, LimitLoadToSessionType Aqua, no node and no other environment. The script names the stable registered wrapper in the gateway state directory, never a release path, and registration refuses any other path; the wrapper is single-quoted for the shell. The script (mode 700) and the plist (mode 600) are private and written atomically, the script first, and the agent is bootstrapped into gui/<uid> when written. An agent written by 0.4.5 or earlier ran launchctl directly; registering again replaces it with the script form. A script at that path without the gateway's marker is refused, like an unmanaged plist. A standalone gateway desktop register writes or updates it, so it follows the registration. A plist with that label that does not carry the gateway's marker is refused, and nothing is changed (on the unified service path it is only reported).

Where the unified service owns the variable (the desktop component's desktop-restore, or a registration while a unified or staged plan owns it) no agent is written, and registration returns envAgent: false and loginEnv: "service", plus envAgentRemoved: true when it removed a 0.4.7 agent. A failure to remove the agent or an unmanaged plist at its label is caught: registration keeps going, and the service records a desktop_env_agent_failed event with a fixed reason (other or unmanaged, see diagnostics), never the error text or a path. The next start tries again. A hand-run gateway desktop register on such a Mac takes the same path and records the event under the component service. Only on a Mac without a unified plan does a hand-run gateway desktop register write the agent, fail loudly when it cannot, and record no event.

The script sets nothing unless the gateway can still run: before the launchctl setenv it checks that the registered wrapper is executable and that the installed release's package/dist/cli.js exists, and otherwise exits 0. A login after the gateway was uninstalled, or unregistered by an older release, therefore does not set the variable again.

API mode

While API mode is on, none of these paths arms the adapter. <state>/api-mode.json is the switch, so the daemon's first-step preset, the desktop-restore child and a hand-run gateway desktop register all hold back: the first two skip and record one desktop_api_mode event (action: "preset", outcome: "skipped") per process, and a hand-run register refuses with "API mode is on; run gateway desktop api-mode off first". Neither the registration receipt nor the service plan is changed by that, because API mode only takes the variable out of the login session; gateway desktop api-mode off puts it back through the same preset. See API mode.

Rollback and removal

Rolling back to 0.4.5 or earlier: those releases do not know this agent, so their gateway desktop unregister and gateway uninstall leave its plist and script behind. Before running either, remove them: launchctl bootout gui/$UID/com.edihasaj.subscription-gateway.desktop-env, then move ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.edihasaj.subscription-gateway.desktop-env.plist and <state>/harness-gateway-login-env to the Trash. Even if you do not, the guard above stops the script from setting the variable once the release is gone.

gateway desktop unregister and gateway uninstall boot the agent out and move its script and plist to the Trash (the script only when it carries the gateway's marker), before they clear the variable. The agent is not a service component: consolidation does not collect or retire it.

Checking login status

gateway desktop status reads CODEX_CLI_PATH from the login (GUI) domain: it parses only that key from the environment block of launchctl print gui/<uid>, and falls back to launchctl getenv only when the print fails. launchctl getenv over SSH reads a different domain and reported activeForFutureLaunches: false even when the login session held the right value. Status also reports envAgent: true when the agent exists, is the gateway's, and its script sets the registered wrapper. loginEnv says who sets the variable at login: "service" when a unified service (or its pending login plan) exists, "agent" when the standalone agent is in place, otherwise "none". forceCliSet and legacyForceCli come from the same block: status keeps only whether CODEX_APP_SERVER_FORCE_CLI is present and non-empty (and whether it is 1), never its value, and uses launchctl getenv for both variables only when the print fails.
